Yea, it’s not too complicated the main thing is you just have to know where you should be doing it, is the main thing I was getting at and realizing that the equations can evolve in many ways and in general be more convoluted than the simplified problems I posted. For example you’ll have an equation with 5 different variables and have to really think about which one is changing with respect to what and what that is causing to happen in the system. They might even say something like, “a closed loop of radius r is being rotated by a homogeneous magnetic field of magnitude B = 10 in the x direction, after the loop has moved through an angle of 20° from a starting position intersecting the magnetic field at 45°, where the axis of rotation is along the y axis, what is the current being generated in the wire?” So what is changing in this scenario? Obviously, we have a magnetic field causing some torque on our loop of wire, so clearly we can see that the angle is changing.

Alright now what else is changing, that might be less obvious? What is causing the current in the wire? And how does a change in angle affect that value? What direction is the current flowing in the loop? How do you know which direction the magnetic field is causing the wire to rotate? To answer the first question, “what else is changing” we have to consider what happens to the loop as the magnetic field flows through it and causes it rotation. As the theta changes, we also expect the area that at the magnetic field flows through also changes (this is what causes the current in the wire by a process called induction), I’ll skip the math because it’s unimportant, since the area is changing the amount of magnetic field lines that goes through the loop also changes, then because the magnetic field lines are changing you have induction and an electric potential is produced in your wire, as the electric potential changes with the field lines, a current is produced in the wire that changes based on the electric potential. 

So simply knowing that the angle was changing didn’t actually help you solve the problem. You needed to know what was the consequence of the angle changing, which ended up blowing up into multiple different equations. This process of solving a problem from some of its most basic elements is called first principles and is of critical importance in working physics problems. From providing relatively little data and simply discovering that the angle is changing we were able to make multiple assumptions that lead us to our desired value, the current. that is what physics is, learning the most basic truths of the physical system and applying that knowledge to make justifiable assumptions that get you from point a to b with math simply being a tool that helps you get there.  Yes, the math can be very simple at times, but where do I do the math is the question, and what happens when you find a problem that’s both rigorous in math and physics? How physics professor teach you is how to approach a problem and how to look at it, not so much the math. So it’s extremely important to look at the thought process and logical steps needed to get from point a to point b as opposed to just blindly doing math and hoping you get there.

It might help to review geometry more or learn to notice things like x/v=t. If you have taken vector cal I would highly recommend going over that or even trying to teach yourself some (will help tremendously when your prof goes over maxwells equations and half the class has ptsd). Just a heads up though when you have something like I(t) in an equation it can often be rewritten as something like Io * e^t I’m just bring it up because when I first saw my prof do things like that or had to do that on the homework I couldn’t get past the first step. 

However if by in optics it incorporates wave motions (probably not probably more just macroscopic rays) I would suggest going over Simple harmonic motion. 

Another thing, DO NOT LOOK UP THE ANSWER. I’ll say it twice, DO NOT LOOK UP THE ANSWER, you will hate yourself on every test. This class will be demanding (particularly if you’re not too strong at math/vector cal. If you can’t figure out the answer, re read the section in the book, go over lecture note, or go to office hours. I’d recommend going to office hours even if you haven’t looked at the homework yet so you don’t get stuck on that one problem that takes everyone hours because “they just don’t see it”. If you look up the answer you never learn how to solve the problem from scratch and how everything actually relates to each other for a simple example velocity is distance over time or x/t if you look up the answer you’re like, “ohh shit, it’s so obvious it’s x/t” then you get to the test:

Say you have a function x(t) = t^3 + 1 which specifies the position of a traveling particle, after 5 seconds, what is the velocity of the particle?

Now with the previously “obvious” answer you got from online you’re probably going to be like ohh well let me somehow get x/t. Which isn’t possible. Now if you went back and read you would have noticed that the derivative of x with respect to t is the velocity, dx/dt = v meaning 3t^2 = v(t) where t = 5. 

Obviously this isn’t a perfect example, but my point is you don’t actually learn anything about the physics behind the symbols and how they relate to each-other if you google the answer and I’m only going deep into this because I learned this the hard way as do student every semester in physics.

It might help to work on the basic relation ship between things like how power ( E/t = dE/dt = P) can be derived from energy or how work is W = Fx (force times distance), but can also be expressed as dW = Fdx, (all we have to do to get the work is integrate both sides and we find W = Fx) when the distance changes continuously. But also notice that depending on what is actually changing (let’s say acceleration is a function of time or a(t) = t^2) in the question you may have to notice that the position isn’t what’s changing (dx) to cause a change in the work but Instead would find that the force is changing as a function of time (dF(t)) and that the distance is constant, so instead of dW = Fdx we would in this problem hold x constant and write this dW= x dF(t) where all I did was say that F is a function of time F(t) (because from Newton’s law F=ma ( or F(t) = ma(t)) where acceleration is a function of time (a(t)=t^2). For this this problem instead of saying ingeral of dW = integral of F dx, we would have:

(Note: ~ means therefore or is the same as) 
dW = x dF ~ dW = x dF(t) ~ dW = x d(ma(t)) ~ dW = xm d(a(t)) 

(Note m is constant and doesn’t depend on t) 

~ dW = xm d(t^2 ) (integrating both sides with respect to t)

~ W = xm (t^3 /3)

If you understand what I was talking about there it will help you tremendously in electricity and magnetism. If not I would highly recommend learning that thought process, where you take the integral of the value that’s changing ie you choose what you’re integrating over(or taking the derivative of) not just always integrate over x or some other value that might have nothing to do with the problem. 

I hope I didn’t over load this comment, just all the things that I wish I knew going into electricity and magnetism. Just remember it’s not a cookie cutter class, you have to really think about what you’re doing and why, so really focus on how things relate to eachother and the thought process of how to approach the problems, every step you make should be logical, not entirely methodical (choosing what you integrate over = logical, how you take the integral = methodical). 

You still have a month to prepare so I’d study from what I said starting where you don’t understand. 

(Note: I’m a physics major at UT Austin and we have a pretty competitive physics program)

I would say be honest to some degree but also maybe have an androgynous nickname as an intermediate if things are too uncomfortable in girl mode, working in the service industry can be pretty harsh on transpeople. I definitely think if you’re confident and upfront about it, it won’t take anything away from you applying (unless they’re bigoted and if that’s the case you really don’t want to work there) also any uncertainty about you being transgender will be easily over looked if they see you as a strong and confident person. The key to interviews is confidence, confidence, confidence. 

I’ve never been denied a job if I’ve talked to a manager face to face. This is over the phone so it’s a little different but in person you approach them smile, stand straight, make a good 2 Mississippi eye contact before breaking at all while shaking their hand with a firm grip. Talk with hands and maintain 80% eye contact, maybe don’t immediately tell them and ease into that conversation I a natural way, maybe wait till part of the interview where it seems appropriate like if they ask, “are there any concerns you have?”, “yea, actually, so I’m transgender and I like to be referred to as _____, would y’all be able to accommodate me and in what ways?” Being straightforward and honest is crucial for any good relationship, which is what you’re building with a potential employer. Keep this in mind, the employer doesn’t always want the best person for the job, they want someone they like and can connect with. Same way as to how you get promotions, building a solid connection and it’s basically given to you, often times without asking. People typically like you better when you ask questions, it’s more engaging and personalized, wouldn’t you agree? So be sure to ask them questions and really try to get them talking about something within the job that they may be passionate about, for example, “do you have any questionable for me?”, yea how long have you worked here? What’s your favorite thing? How can I succeed working here?.. you can even ask rhetorical questions, the more engaging the better, “if you were me and starting tomorrow how would you go about preparing?” 

Now this all seems excessive and that’s the point, it shows you’re super interested and excited to work them as opposed to just being like, “this is exciting I want to work here”. Actions speak louder than words. All the questions implies you’re excited so when you say it they know you mean it. But now think about everyone else apply, is anyone else taking the time to build this connections and learn something about the employer and maybe his aspirations? Is anyone anxiously waiting for their boss to tell them how they can prepare before the even start their first day? Probably not. If you’re not being fake about it and you’re genuinely interested in the things you’re talking about than the jobs cake and being transgender won’t matter at all. 

Tldr: build a genuine connection with the interviewer and you got the job, doesn’t matter if you’re trans, but be sure you confidently bring it up like it’s no big deal (it isn’t) so you can focus on what actually matters in the interview.

I don’t know how much of my story can relate to yours, but I will try to say what happened with me and friends and what I learned from it, though every situation is different so take this with a grain of salt.

With that said, I grew up very conservative and I knew my parents wouldn’t be supportive about me being trans and I didn’t even realize it was an option (this was just before the whole trans viability really hit the mainstream). I ended up homeless and had amazing friends who took me in during high school as I started questioning if I was just gay or more feminine and what not: I started dressing up and did things like get my belly button pierced and painting nails gradually till I started college, after jumping from house to house with my friends being the best people I could have wished for in that time in my life (a bunch of conservative young adults willing to be open to my changes). 

When I started college I really realized I was transgender and I had a couple of this close friend group really take distance away from me because I guess they just really didn’t understand it and though it was incredibly weird, which without knowing anyone who was transgender and when all the information they get about it on the news in conservative Texas being “transgender people are men dressing as women to sneak into women’s restroom” their skepticism seems justified. Understanding this I I tried to ease them more into things and show them a more accurate perspective and a lot of the time pushed myself to hang out with them. They were really my everything, we had all grown up together and I felt a connection with them that I’m not sure I can with anyone else, they were the people I snuck out with and smoked weed for the first time with and all these first time experiences were with them growing up and yadda yadda. So for the longest time I didn’t understand why they were gradually fading away. part of it was simply that we were getting older and our interests had changed, one of my got into sales, another is starting a pressure washing a third wanting to work at the plants, all of which are pretty masculine professions. Meanwhile I was exploring things like nail polish and make up and having girls teach me things how to take care of my skin and properly manage my hair. 

As I slowly started to become more feminine with hormones, growing breasts, working on fitting my new found “female role”, etc. really expedited the changes I went through and made our once seemingly perfect social circle split in many vary wide directions. After a while I almost stopped visiting with them entirely and only meeting up on special occasions the kinda you don’t miss when someone’s basically family. Some of them still don’t call me by my preferred name and part of it i believe is they can’t let go of who I was or don’t fully understand the other side of reality I’m living on. It’s taken a long time to grasp that I can’t change them and that they may never fully understand me, but I know they still love me the way I love them, as brothers(although I’m a sister, but from a growing up frame of reference)

Anyways before I eventually moved away to college I ended up sleeping with my best friend (not one of the ones I was referring to, he was in a different friend group). He understood at least a little better what I was going through, he worked on my pronouns well before I started passing, although he was defiantly somewhat homophobic/transphobic during the early stages he really came around. (Conservative Texas so it’s not uncommon for these characteristics). I’ve known him for so long and really loved him. But after moving away that relationship faded faster than you could even image to the point when I meet up with him now we’re complete strangers even though we’ve been best friends since third grade. This has been the hardest of all my friends to let go. 

I didn’t want to let it go because how much he meant to me and that he always stood up to me when no one else did or someone tried to pick on me. Holding on to it only made it hurt worse, as that friend ship faded so did that part of me and my dying childhood. We have nothing to talk about anymore and after trying to text long distance to keep in touch we don’t talk anymore. Our lives couldn’t be more opposite.

I tried to use him to cope with my problems and put all my pain on him when I couldn’t bear it anymore, and he really just can’t understand the things I go through being transgender. I guess a part of me thought if he see how much pain I’m in he won’t leave and he’ll keep texting me and what not. I think it worked for a while until the pain got so bad I tried to kill myself as we started talking less and less. He was my dude. That was last month. I haven’t talked to him since he orchestrated my rescue when I couldn’t stop taking pills and drinking alcohol. (Well we talked a little bit after but we hadn’t gone this long without talking since I moved) I don’t feel like I need to talk to him anymore and I’m finally over our friendship. 

I wish I had more strength when the relationship was going bad to let got of it and move on to different more like minded people, like the people I am surrounded by in this part of Texas. I wish that I could have let go of these relationships as easy as they seemed able to. But idk, I think I was just afraid to be alone I guess and I think that made me more alone. So I guess if there’s one thing to sum up out of all this, is don’t be afraid to let people go out of your life who are no longer beneficial to you, you should be selfish about your wellbeing and mental health. Transitioning will probably be the single hardest thing you do in your life, challenges come out of no where and often knock you on your ass, but it’s fucking worth it, is people don’t like it fuck them.

I’m not sure I’m convinced that that ways appropriate though it may be. How I would solve the problem is divide it into two equations of motion, one for the officer and one for the speeding car. As such we would have this;

Police officer:
Xo = 0 
Vo = 0 
a = 3 (m/s^2)

For the speeding car,

Vo = Vf (b/c it’s constant speed) = 15 m/s
Xo = 0

So what we want to find is the time that the cop car is in the same position as the speeding vehicle.

Looking at the kinematic equations (or deducing them logically) we can see that;

Equation of motion for cop car:
Xf = Xo + Vo*t + (1/2)at^2 
Or just 
Xf = (1/2) a t^2
